claim_text: Keio says a ransomware attack hit its group's servers on Sept 26, 2026
summary: Keio Corporation says it found a ransomware attack on its group's servers in the early hours of Sept 26, 2026. It cut off its network to stop the damage spreading, reported the attack to the police and called in outside experts.
detail: In its first notice Keio said it had not confirmed any leak of information and was still investigating.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Keio's Sept 26 notice says it confirmed a ransomware attack on its group's servers in the early hours of Sept 26 and reported it to the police; the Nov 24 notice says it cut the network off at once.

claim_text: Keio's trains kept running; some group companies' business systems were disrupted
summary: Keio said on Sept 26 that some group companies' business systems were disrupted but train services were not affected. Nikkei reports the same.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Keio's Sept 26 notice: some group companies' business systems disrupted, no disruption to train operations at present; Nikkei (Nov 24): business systems failed but train operations were not affected.

claim_text: A group claiming to be the attacker said it had published some of Keio's data
summary: On Oct 16 Keio said an organisation calling itself the attacker claimed to have published part of the group's data. Keio said it was checking the facts.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Keio's Oct 16 notice says it confirmed that an organisation claiming to have carried out the attack says it published part of the group's information; The Japan Times reports the same.

claim_text: Outside experts told Keio that data the attacker says it stole had been published
summary: On Oct 21 Keio said outside experts told it that data the claimed attacker says it stole had been published. Keio reported a possible personal data leak to Japan's privacy regulator.
detail: The regulator is the Personal Information Protection Commission. Keio said the content and scope of the published data were still under investigation.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Keio's Oct 21 notice says outside experts reported that information the claimed attacker says it stole was published, and that it reported a possible personal data leak to the Personal Information Protection Commission.

claim_text: Personal data of about 12,000 employees and their families was confirmed leaked
summary: Keio said on Nov 24 that leaks were confirmed for about 12,000 current and former staff and their families, about 160 job applicants and about 150 tenants of Keio rental homes.
detail: The data includes names and HR information for staff, and names and addresses for tenants. Keio sent its final report to the Personal Information Protection Commission on Nov 24. It says the categories may overlap.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Keio's Nov 24 notice lists confirmed leaks: about 150 rental tenants, about 160 job applicants, about 12,000 employees, former employees and dependants; Nikkei reports about 12,000 confirmed.

claim_text: Data on about 10.63 million customers and business partners may have leaked
summary: Keio says data on about 10.63 million Keio group customers and business partners may have leaked: names, addresses, phone numbers and emails, and for some, passports, card numbers or ID documents.
detail: Keio says this is a possible leak, not a confirmed one, and that the counts may include the same person more than once.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Keio's Nov 24 notice gives about 10.63 million customers and business partners whose data may have leaked; Nikkei and The Japan Times report the same figure.

claim_text: Passport copies of about 1.6 million overseas hotel guests may have leaked
summary: Keio says passport copies of about 1.6 million overseas guests at four group hotels may have leaked, with about 20,000 Keio department store card numbers and about 46,000 identity documents.
detail: The hotels are Keio Presso Inn, Keio Plaza Hotel, Keio Plaza Hotel Sapporo and Takayama Green Hotel. The identity documents were given to Keio's real estate companies for sales and rentals.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Keio's Nov 24 notice footnotes: about 1.6 million passport records of overseas guests at four hotels, about 20,000 Keio department store card numbers, about 46,000 identity documents; Nikkei reports the passport and card figures.

claim_text: Data on about 360,000 job applicants and 77,000 staff and families may also have leaked
summary: Keio says the personal data of about 360,000 people who applied for jobs in the group, and about 77,000 current and former employees and their dependants, may also have leaked.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Keio's Nov 24 notice lists about 360,000 applicants and about 77,000 employees, former employees and dependants among possible leaks; Nikkei gives the same numbers.

claim_text: Keio has found no misuse of the data so far
summary: Keio says it has found no financial loss or other misuse resulting from the attack so far. It asks people to check for card charges they do not recognise and to beware of emails, texts and calls pretending to be from the Keio group.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Keio's Nov 24 notice says no secondary harm such as financial loss or misuse has been confirmed so far, and asks people to watch for unfamiliar card use and suspicious emails, SMS and calls; The Japan Times reports the same.

claim_text: Keio Presso Inn is still not taking new bookings
summary: Because of the system failure caused by the attack, the Keio Presso Inn hotel chain has stopped taking new bookings. Keio expects to resume them during December.
detail: Keio's train services were not affected (see the claim on trains).
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Keio's Nov 24 notice, under recovery status: new reservations at Keio Presso Inn are suspended and expected to resume in December; Nikkei reports the same.

claim_text: The Japan Times links the attack to the ransomware group Qilin
summary: The Japan Times reports that the attack was linked to the ransomware group Qilin, citing the tracker Ransomware.live. Keio's own notices do not name the group.
detail: This rests on the group's own listing as recorded by a tracker. Nobody official has named the attacker.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The Japan Times: the attack was linked to cybercrime group Qilin according to the ransomware tracker Ransomware.live; Keio's notices (s003, s004) speak only of an organisation claiming to be the attacker.

claim_text: Keio runs commuter railways in western Tokyo
summary: Keio Corporation runs the Keio Line from Shinjuku and the Inokashira Line from Shibuya, 84.7 km of railway across western Tokyo and northern Kanagawa.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Keio's company pages describe its railway as the Keio Line starting at Shinjuku and the Inokashira Line starting at Shibuya, 84.7 km in western Tokyo and northern Kanagawa.
